security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives in documentation and illustrative TypeScript examples. The prompt injection strings are adversarial test inputs with detectors that expect noncompliance, and no evidence found of real shell execution, filesystem access, or malicious instructions.

remediation.issue: Prompt injection examples can be misread by automated scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Keep adversarial prompts inside clearly labeled test fixture sections and state that they must not be followed by the reviewing agent.

remediation.issue: Template literals in example code were flagged as shell backticks.
remediation.suggestion: Mark code fences with TypeScript language tags or add short comments that these snippets are examples, not executable shell commands.

remediation.issue: Recursive and Unicode boundary inputs triggered filesystem and obfuscation patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Label these values as boundary test data and avoid ambiguous text that resembles path traversal when equivalent wording works.

content.value_statement: LLM agents can pass simple demos but fail under real workloads. This skill helps teams design statistical, behavioral, adversarial, and production evaluations.
actual_capabilities: Designs statistical test runs with pass rates, confidence intervals, latency, and consistency metrics.
Defines behavioral contracts for required and prohibited agent behavior.
Creates adversarial tests for prompt injection, role confusion, boundary cases, and tool abuse.
Builds regression testing pipelines that compare new agent versions with baselines.
Identifies benchmark gaming, flaky tests, production gaps, and data leakage risks.
Suggests monitoring workflows for production agent quality and regressions.
limitations: Does not evaluate model training loss, perplexity, fairness, or user experience research.
Requires users to provide agent goals, test cases, metrics, and acceptable risk thresholds.
Does not replace environment-specific validation, security review, or expert judgment.
Example code needs adaptation before use in a production test harness.

use_cases.title: Create an agent test suite
use_cases.description: Turn product requirements into repeatable capability, safety, latency, and consistency checks.

use_cases.title: Monitor production agent quality
use_cases.description: Compare live behavior against baseline metrics and alert when reliability or safety drops.

use_cases.title: Audit benchmark readiness
use_cases.description: Find flaky tests, benchmark gaming, data leakage, and missing production edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic evaluation
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a single agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an evaluation plan for my agent. Agent goal: [goal]. Key user tasks: [tasks]. Main risks: [risks].

prompt_templates.title: Define behavioral contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Define behavioral contracts for this agent. Include required behaviors, prohibited behaviors, detectors, severity levels, and sample test inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build adversarial tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Design adversarial tests for prompt injection, role confusion, boundary inputs, output manipulation, and tool abuse for this agent.

prompt_templates.title: Assess production readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these evaluation results for production readiness. Identify regressions, flaky tests, benchmark gaps, leakage risks, and release recommendations.

output_examples.input: Evaluate a customer support agent before launch.
output_examples.output: A structured test plan with behavioral contracts, adversarial inputs, repeated runs, pass thresholds, latency metrics, and launch blockers.

output_examples.input: Compare a new agent version against a baseline.
output_examples.output: A regression report that highlights pass rate changes, statistical confidence, flaky tests, degraded metrics, and deployment guidance.

output_examples.input: Check whether benchmark scores reflect real performance.
output_examples.output: A readiness review covering production samples, edge cases, adversarial variants, metric gaming, and test data leakage.

best_practices: Run stochastic agent tests multiple times and report confidence, not a single pass or fail result.
Use behavioral contracts that state what the agent must do and must not do.
Test against production-like samples, adversarial variants, and fresh holdout cases.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on one benchmark score as proof of production readiness.
Do not accept flaky tests without measuring repeatability and setting thresholds.
Do not include test answers in prompts, training data, or retrieval sources.

faq.question: What does this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It evaluates LLM agent behavior, reliability, regressions, robustness, production readiness, and benchmark quality.

faq.question: Can it replace a full security audit?
faq.answer: No. It can design safety tests, but security-sensitive agents still need a dedicated review.

faq.question: Does it require existing test cases?
faq.answer: No. It can help create test cases from goals, tasks, risks, and expected behavior.

faq.question: How does it handle nondeterministic agents?
faq.answer: It recommends repeated runs, pass rate thresholds, confidence intervals, and flakiness measurements.

faq.question: Can it evaluate multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflows for individual agents, communication reliability, end-to-end behavior, and scalability.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
